take_homes: The agent-risk audit on my own system gave me a ranked list and an uncomfortable feeling, so now I have specific risks to look at.
The check is a saved skill with a policy lens and an agent-risk lens. I can rerun it, improve it, and give it to a teammate.

Agents are a different kind of security problem because the attack is words in a document the agent reads. The best mitigation is the access I don't grant, and the rest goes to a person who owns that area.

monday.move: Run the agent-audit skill against the pricing-pilot brief setup, pick the top risk, scope that access down, and bring any remaining 'I can't tell' rows to legal or IT
monday.who: Me first, then one person from my team of fourteen who gets the skill installed
monday.when: Monday morning before the pricing working group sync
monday.stop_condition: One risk is mitigated, the residual is written down, and the open questions are with legal or IT
monday.blocker: My team has no shared place for the skill and context files, so everyone would install their own copy. Customer data in the pricing sources may also need legal sign-off.

misconception.why: What made the check good was my own lines about what matters at Nordveil, and the saved skill I can hand to a teammate. Better prompts had little to do with it. I still half-think prompt skill matters.

one_line: The hands-on audit of my own system was worth the time, but the same filler paragraph shows up nine times and you can cut all of it.
